data.narrative:
Reditus Space is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Stef Crum (PhD in Space Systems Engineering, former NASA and Space Force orbital operations specialist) and Will Sherman (aerospace engineer). The company has raised $7.1M to date. The space and aerospace sector comprises 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though few operate at the seed stage.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression triangulation proved applicable. This method uses total capital raised ($7.1M) as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.5x multiplier representing typical step-ups from seed to series A funding. This yields an implied valuation of $17.75M. Peer-median analysis could not be performed due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables in space and aerospace (zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage datapoints). Public-comp anchoring was inapplicable because the target's revenue is not disclosed, precluding use of the sector median P/S multiple of 27.4x across public names.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $20M, with a median point of $18M. However, this reflects a single method and should be weighted accordingly. Key uncertainties include the lack of revenue disclosure, absence of seed-stage peer transaction data in the sector, and unknown customer traction or technical milestones. Additional disclosure of early revenue or customer commitments would materially strengthen the valuation case.
